name: Special education initial evaluation deadlines by state — days, day type, and what starts the clock
description: The legal deadline for completing an initial special education evaluation under the IDEA, per state: how many days, whether those are calendar, school or business days, what event starts the clock, the separate deadline for the eligibility meeting or the first IEP, and how school vacations are counted. Federal 34 CFR 300.301(c)(1) says 60 days from parental consent unless the state sets its own timeframe — and most states do. Minnesota allows 30 school days, Texas 45 school days, Illinois 60 school days, Pennsylvania 60 calendar days excluding the summer, Virginia 65 business days measured from the referral rather than from consent, and Washington moved to 35 school days on 11 June 2026. Answers 'how long does the school have to evaluate my child in [state]' and 'is the 60-day rule calendar days or school days here', which are the questions parents ask when a district has gone quiet.
licence: State statutes and regulations plus the federal IDEA regulation; statutory deadlines are facts and are not copyrightable, quoted with citation to the publishing authority.

(3) When the student is to be evaluated to determine eligibility for special education services and the educational needs of the student, the school district shall provide prior written notice to the parent, attempt without unnecessary delay to obtain consent, fully evaluate the student and arrive at a decision regarding eligibility within: (a) Thirty-five school days after the date written consent for an evaluation has been provided to the school district by the parent; or

Districts must complete an initial special education evaluation or reevaluation to determine the eligibility or continuing eligibility of a student for special education services within 35 school days of receiving written consent from the parent.

The district must then convene an eligibility determination meeting to review the results in the evaluation report and determine the student’s eligibility (or continuing eligibility) for special education services no sooner than five school days after the evaluation report is provided to the parent and no later than 40 school days following the receipt of the parent consent.
